TomTom Expands EV Charger Data Past 2 Million Points

2026-09-08 The EV Report Staff TomTom, EV charging, 2 million chargers, availability profiles, live pricing, AI range prediction, super aggregator, Drew Meehan, EV POI data, charging infrastructure
Read the source article

Quick summary

TomTom now covers more than two million EV charging points globally and plans to ship an AI-based battery range prediction model by the end of 2026, as the company reports delivering on its two-year EV roadmap with overhauled POI data, availability profiles, and live pricing.

Key takeaways

  • TomTom's EV charging data now covers over 2 million charging points globally
  • Availability profiles use six weeks of rolling usage data to predict charger busyness at expected arrival time
  • A "super aggregator" model works with regional data partners rather than connecting to every charge point operator individually
  • Driver demand has shifted from finding a charger to choosing one based on price, amenities, security, and weather protection
  • An AI-based range prediction API is on track for release by end of 2026, using learning models trained on actual usage data
  • The EV product group has been reorganized as Destination and Waypoint Management, expanding to cover POI search, fuel prices, parking, and in-car transactions
  • Vehicle-to-grid and vehicle-to-load functions are flagged as growing in importance, but driver experience must be reliable
